mechanisms.name: Inventory-aware intent filling versus ordinary filling plus independent rebalancing
mechanisms.classification: conditional operational optimization; no separate payer or incremental net profit established
mechanisms.economic_cause: Destination inventory is fronted before reimbursement; repayment-location and withdrawal-frequency choices can reduce relocation and funding costs.
mechanisms.payer_and_repeatability: Users pay ordinary execution/settlement spread. Opposite-direction flow may reduce inventory imbalance. No separate inventory-service customer, recurring accessible flow or independent rebate was established.
mechanisms.asset_claim_equivalence: Verify exact source/destination/refund token contracts and redemption rights. A Hub balance is a protocol claim, not wallet tokens; USDC.e is not Circle-native USDC. No present route mapping was independently verified.
mechanisms.deployment_evidence: Current provider descriptions of Across V3-style mechanics and Relay Settlement; no contract addresses, deployed-version reconciliation, balances, admission or executed quote independently checked.
chain_contexts: Across origin/destination, repayment chain and Ethereum HubPool/canonical bridge dependencies
Relay origin/destination, Relay Chain and Aurora/NEAR Allocator dependencies; exact distinct-chain count unresolved
inventory_lifecycle: Reserve spendable destination token inventory and gas.
Front q to the destination user; record pending receivable, not revenue or free capital.
Across: validate fill/deposit, propose/challenge bundle, transmit roots, execute relayer refund on chosen chain.
Relay: attest fill/deposit, credit Hub, select withdrawal parameters, authorize and obtain MPC proof, release actual Depository tokens.
Rebalance or match independently available opposite flow; retire borrowing if used.
Close same terminal chain/token inventory, liabilities and unresolved claims as comparator.

accounting.profit_identity: V(actual net reimbursement)-V(destination output)-all nonembedded gas/rebalance/funding/failure/inventory/access costs+proven separate payments
accounting.incremental_identity: difference in net reimbursements minus difference in all costs plus difference in proven separate payments; same fills and terminal inventories
double_counting_prohibitions: Do not add ordinary fill margin, quoted capital compensation and the same input-output spread as separate revenues.
Do not subtract embedded LP deductions twice or add a refund of principal as profit.
Do not assign integrator appFee to the relayer without proving recipient ownership and actual payment.
Do not fund overlapping obligations from the same pending refund or undisbursed credit.

capital_assumptions: Only available settled balances or actually disbursed credit fund obligations.
Count liabilities, collateral and pending protocol claims; no automatic debt netting against common-failure exposure.
Original 50k equity, 15k common-domain, <=3-chain and <=2x delta-neutral leverage gates remain unresolved.
costs_and_risks: Location-dependent LP fees and exact refund deductions
Independent bridge/swap slippage, time and representation risk
Funding interest, collateral/liquidation, access and operating costs
mechanisms.lock_time: First irrevocable capital commitment to spendable return in required chain/token. Neither Across minimum ~1.5h proposal cadence nor Relay real-time Hub credit is a measured or guaranteed capital-lock bound.
mechanisms.recent_change_assessment: Relay Vaults currently disallows new deposits; dated wind-down start unknown. Across now documents Solana destination app-fee recipients but launch date/deployment not verified. Circle 2026 credit facilities are contractual and no direct integration was established.
cheap_falsifiers: Stop new-depositor Relay Vaults branch based on official no-new-deposits notice.
Establish one eligible order route, solver access and exact beneficiaries before collecting performance history.
For same accessible fills and terminal inventories require positive incremental net after all repayment-location and rebalancing costs.
Verify withdrawal spendability and common dependencies; reject concurrent reuse of pending principal.

mechanisms.name: Collateralized temporary inventory replacement while a bridge leg is pending
mechanisms.classification: historical paper mechanism with current financing analogues; not a flash loan
mechanisms.economic_cause: Borrow exact expensive-chain sale asset to reduce time between price-dislocated trade legs; bridge purchased cheap-chain asset to repay later.
mechanisms.payer_and_repeatability: Price-takers sustaining a cross-chain dislocation may fund a gross spread; competition and financing can consume it. No current repeatable dislocation observed.
mechanisms.asset_claim_equivalence: Incoming bridged asset must exactly repay debt token; wrapper, gateway, decimals and redemption claims must match.
mechanisms.deployment_evidence: Seed Appendix G reports Ethereum WBTC purchase, Arbitrum Aave borrow/sale and later arrival/repayment. Historical transaction links are retained in sources.json; not independently rechecked. Current borrowing caps/health factors unknown.
financing_inventory_lifecycle: Preposition eligible collateral or obtain an approved contractual line.
Buy cheaper asset and initiate bridge.
Borrow matching destination debt asset, sell there.
Receive exact repayment asset and retire principal plus all costs.
Release collateral only after obligations close.
capital_assumptions: Collateral and credit capacity are economic capital, even if already held.
No free flash-loan funding across non-atomic chains.
No qualifying 2x leverage or common-domain compliance established.
costs_and_risks: Borrow rate, liquidation/oracle risk and collateral opportunity cost
Bridge arrival/representation mismatch, paused borrowing or caps
All execution, settlement and failed-leg costs
cheap_falsifiers: Reject if borrowed token cannot be repaid by the bridged claim.
Compare full collateral/debt lifecycle against prepositioned inventory, not just trade-leg delay.

mechanisms.name: Native-versus-canonical bridged stablecoin conversion basis
mechanisms.classification: conditional liquidity/redemption risk premium, no observed spread
mechanisms.economic_cause: Holders may pay for liquidity in the preferred token representation while a discounted wrapper has a slower redemption path.
mechanisms.payer_and_repeatability: Urgent liquidity users might pay the basis; issuer/bridge risk and competition can fully explain it. Current payer, quote and recurring volume unknown.
mechanisms.asset_claim_equivalence: Arbitrum native USDC 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 differs from USDC.e 0xff970a61a04b1ca14834a43f5de4533ebddb5cc8. Canonical redemption and native burn/mint are distinct legs; no permissionless par conversion or personal Mint redemption right assumed.
mechanisms.deployment_evidence: Public token addresses and documented canonical/CCTP distinction. No current gateway escrow/contract mapping, caps or pool state checked.
financing_inventory_lifecycle: Acquire a specifically discounted claim only if exact redemption path is established.
Convert into the exact native sale/debt token using a supported route.
Close all hedge/debt/rebalance legs and terminal inventory.
capital_assumptions: <=3 selected chains and 15k issuer/bridge/common-domain ceiling apply to full lifecycle.
Returned claims and sale proceeds cannot both be counted as free inventory.
costs_and_risks: Slow redemption and separate claim gas
Issuer eligibility/freeze, bridge collateral and representation mismatch
Swap/route fees, CCTP deployment-specific fees, funding and competing conversions
cheap_falsifiers: No current actionable discounted quote means no demonstrated trade.
Reject a supposed shortcut that burns USDC.e in native USDC CCTP or assumes symbol equivalence.
Check exact claim and personal redemption eligibility before a price comparison.

mechanisms.name: Contractual RWA redemption or settlement advance
mechanisms.classification: recent provider-released institutional financing instrument, not open arbitrage
mechanisms.economic_cause: Funding bridges time from an Arc token burn/redemption or slow fiat settlement into available USD/USDC.
mechanisms.payer_and_repeatability: Eligible institutions pay draw/recurring credit fees for working capital. No investment return or independently paying inventory-service customer established.
mechanisms.asset_claim_equivalence: An RWA burn receipt, a credit-line receivable, USD funding and onchain USDC delivery are different claims; funding does not prove underlying asset redeemability or par value.
mechanisms.deployment_evidence: Circle release records list 2026-04-01 Credit API and 2026-10-19 RWA Redemption Advance. Provider release claim, not independent onchain activity or user entitlement.
financing_inventory_lifecycle: Execute Core API Agreement and separate credit contract; enable entitlement.
Reserve line capacity, submit Arc burn hash and proof; Treasury approves or rejects.
Wait for actual disbursement and any separate Credit Express destination delivery.
Maintain required wallet balance, pay draw/recurring fees and repay by contractual deadline.
mechanisms.access: No user agreement, approval, entitlement, limit, fees or disbursement timing established; not assumed available to a 50k entrant.
capital_assumptions: Minimum wallet balance and credit liabilities reduce usable capital.
New Arc exposure, protocol maturity/TVL/audit and <=3-chain/common-domain gates remain unverified.
costs_and_risks: Manual approval/rejection, expired reservation and delivery failure
Issuer, fiat settlement, collateral and default/overdue risk
cheap_falsifiers: Establish lawful institutional eligibility and real terms before any implementation.
Reject if fee/deadline or redemption risk dominates the working-capital benefit.

mechanisms.name: Direction- and representation-aware NEAR settlement routing
mechanisms.classification: non-EVM enabling rail, not observed arbitrage
mechanisms.economic_cause: Different finality/signature/verification paths can change inventory lock and liquidity-service cost.
mechanisms.payer_and_repeatability: Users may pay for faster liquidity; a cheaper route can instead eliminate the old premium. No actual token-specific spread or payer observed.
mechanisms.asset_claim_equivalence: Need exact origin token, NEAR token account and destination representation; local NEP-141 refund atomicity does not imply global rollback.
mechanisms.deployment_evidence: Current official architecture identifies omni.bridge.near and heterogeneous light-client, Wormhole and MPC verification plus Chain Signatures. No route deployment date, token mapping or current activity independently checked.
financing_inventory_lifecycle: Select at most three asset venues and verify exact token routes.
Lock/burn source token; wait for the specified verifier and signature path.
Mint/release destination token; close any fronted inventory or borrowing.
capital_assumptions: Pending bridge messages are not spendable inventory.
All chain/verifier/bridge/issuer domains must be included in concentration and maturity checks.
costs_and_risks: Exact claim mismatch, mint/release limits, destination gas and depth
cheap_falsifiers: First establish token equivalence and one real route; stop if proposed arbitrage only compares names or old timing tables.
Do not infer deployment age from a docs update timestamp.
